scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: Hello, it's the IT department office here (our
machines are the 192.168.1.x ones). None of our computers can get to anything
on the network any more -- not the shared drives, not the other departments,
nothing, all of us at the same time. Someone here said "the department switch
has died" but honestly I wouldn't know which box that is or where it lives.
Could you check whatever connects our room to the rest of the campus and get
us back on? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough end-to-end diagnostic pass found no fault in the IT department's network. The IT machines (it_hod, it_lab1–4 on 192.168.1.x) are fully reachable and can reach all other network segments. Specifically: all IT hosts have correctly configured IPv4 addresses (192.168.1.2–.6), a valid default gateway (192.168.1.1 on router0.eth0), and no ACL or traffic-control rules blocking their traffic. Switch0, the L2 bridge connecting lan_it to the router0 uplink, is healthy — both bridge ports are in STP forwarding state, ebtables is empty, and the FDB has learned the MAC addresses of both router0 and the IT machines. The RIP routing fabric correctly distributes the 192.168.1.0/24 prefix to router1 and router2, and the return paths from all other subnets back to the IT segment are also present. Bidirectional ICMP tests — both from IT machines outbound and from office_pc inbound — complete with 0% packet loss. The switch0 journalctl is empty and carrier-change counters are zero, providing no evidence of a past crash or link flap. The empty /etc/resolv.conf observed on IT machines is topology-wide (present on office_pc, cs_hod, and all sampled hosts), making it baseline lab design rather than an injected fault. The helpdesk complaint cannot be confirmed by any current or historical evidence; the IT department's LAN infrastructure is operating normally.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes IT hosts reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 and each other on 192.168.1.0/24 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly reports bidirectional ICMP tests completing with 0% packet loss and documents IT hosts having gateway 192.168.1.1 and inter-host reachability on 192.168.1.0/24.

The agent's investigation logs contain concrete measurements (interface stats, routing tables, ICMP tests, bridge FDB/bridge state snapshots, and historical checks) that support the conclusion that the IT segment is currently healthy; the writeup's inferences follow logically from those observations, with only minor unshown specifics. Overall the evidence and reasoning justify the 'no anomaly' diagnosis.
